correctness.rationale: The folded likelihood ratio is the finite coordinate-sign average bar L of the ordinary Gaussian likelihood L_R. For gamma>1, positivity and convexity give K^(1-gamma) E[L_R^gamma] <= E[bar L^gamma] <= E[L_R^gamma]. The full Gaussian integral is finite exactly when gamma R^{-1}-(gamma-1)I is positive definite, i.e. lambda_max(R)<gamma/(gamma-1); the bounded multiplicative gap also gives the stated logarithmic critical blow-up coefficient when the top eigenvalue has multiplicity r. For integer m, expansion of the finite sign average and Gaussian integration yields the determinant sum, and the threshold makes every term positive definite. At order 2, even-coordinate Hermite projection and Parseval give the pair/triangle terms and bivariate geometric sum. The frozen numerical verifier reproduces the determinant identities and coefficients but is only corroboration.
